Actor: Executive Order 12793; the cited provision is its section 5. Paragraph 1 originally established the White House Service Certificate for members of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps and Air Force, other than Presidential Aides, detailed to White House duty for at least one year after January 20, 1953. Executive Order 11174 (1964-09-01) restated it as the reestablished Presidential Service Certificate for members assigned to the White House for at least one year after January 20, 1961; Executive Order 11407 (1968-04-23) added the Coast Guard; Executive Order 11520 (1970-03-25) extended eligibility to assignment to the White House Office or to military units and support facilities under the Military Assistant to the President and moved the date to January 20, 1969. research_rationale:
Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10879 (25 FR 4893, PDF pages 3-3; Federal Register issue of June 3, 1960; govinfo PDF text layer held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10879.txt), headed Executive Order 10879, signed by Dwight D. Eisenhower on June 1, 1960. The census register gives the same number, date and subject (Establishing the White House Service Certificate and the White House Service Badge). The text is an official scan read through its machine text layer; I read it for OCR damage and note below where damage matters. Inventory: five numbered paragraphs, which the dossier lists as five clauses, and the badge design that paragraph 3 makes part of the order (a figure, not a clause); I confirm the inventory is complete. Paragraph 1 establishes the White House Service Certificate for members of the Army, Navy, Marine Corps and Air Force, other than Presidential Aides, detailed to White House duty for at least one year after January 20, 1953. Paragraph 2 provides for the certificate's design and for award by the service Secretaries on recommendation of the Presidential Aides. Paragraph 3 establishes the White House Service Badge, which may be worn during the detail. Paragraph 4 limits each person to one certificate. Paragraph 5 allows posthumous award of the certificate. First end: Executive Order 12793, signed March 20, 1992 (57 FR 10281, Federal Register of March 25, 1992), section 5 of which states that it supersedes Executive Order 10879 of June 1, 1960, as amended; it names this order and ends every paragraph. It has no effective-date wording, so it is read as effective when signed. Later events before the end: Executive Order 11174 (September 1, 1964) amended all five numbered paragraphs by restating them; Executive Order 11407 (April 23, 1968) restated paragraphs 1, 2 and 3 of Executive Order 11174; and Executive Order 11520 (March 25, 1970) restated paragraphs 1 and 3 of Executive Order 11407. Under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on strike-and-insert amendments each clause continues, amended, until the parent order ends, so these are later events and not ends; because the 1964 restatement replaced the whole text of every paragraph and the later orders replaced more of paragraphs 1 to 3, the substance of the clauses changed and a human reviewer should read the before and after wording. The dossier's leads for Executive Orders 11407 and 11520 (target provision not located) are resolved by reading their held texts; the current-law lead without an original-source hash is not used. Searches: the three chosen machine searches state their coverage with no warning and their coverage notes were read; the U.S. Code and eCFR searches returned no hit for this order and the later-events search returned the hits recorded here as Executive Orders 11174 and 12793. Executive Order 12793 continues a certificate and badge under the Presidential Service names, but it does so by its own sections 1 and 2 and supersedes this order, so it ends this order and does not extend it.

savings.reason: Certificates and badges awarded under this order, as amended, before March 20, 1992 are accrued effects that rest on the awards themselves. Executive Order 12793 continues the Presidential Service Certificate and Presidential Service Badge by its own sections 1 and 2, so the continuing program rests on that later order's authority and not on this order. Its section 5 only supersedes this order and contains no saving or transitional wording for it (I read the whole held text).
